# dsh-session-delete
English | 中文
A **DeepSeek Harness** (DSH) plugin that adds a genuinely destructive "Delete session" action to the
sidebar session row. After you confirm, it removes that session — **and every subagent session spaw
ned from it** — from disk: the log directory, the projection cache, and the workspace accounting. No
t just hidden from the list.
DSH's built-in "Archive" merely moves a session out of view; the records under `~/.dsh/sessions/` st
ay exactly where they were. When you actually want a session gone locally, this is the missing actio
exactly where they were. When you actually want a session gone locally, this is the missing action.
## What it deletes
A single delete touches exactly three places, all inside `$DSH_HOME` (defaults to `~/.dsh`):
| Location | Contents |
| `sessions/<project-key>/<session-segment>/` | The session log directory, including all subagent se

ssions — usually just a `session.v4.jsonl.zstd` |
| `storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.json`
| The session's projection cache, both the `session-` prefixed and unprefixed historical spellings |
| `storages/workspace.json` | Drops the id from `sessionIds`, `archivedSessionIds`, and `pinnedSess
ges/workspace.json` | Drops the id from `sessionIds`, `archivedSessionIds`, and `pinnedSessionIds` |
Subagent sessions are discovered through the `parentSession` field on persistence headers and live s
ession headers — never through the UI's collapse state. The order is load-bearing: **stop live work
→ delete from disk → strip accounting**. Reverse it and a running turn writes the state straight bac
k while you are deleting.
## What it deliberately leaves alone
- **The workspace directory itself** and every file in it. Your code, notes, and build artifacts are

untouched, byte for byte.
- **The `attachments/` content-addressed store.** One image may be refere

nced by several sessions; deleting it would break the others.
- **Any other session's data.**
- **Wo
rkspace records inside `workspace.json`.** The workspace stays; it just holds one fewer session.

## Usage

1. Find the target session in the sidebar.
2. Click that row's **"…"** button, or just **right-click

** the row — right-click opens the very same native menu.
3. Choose **Delete session**.
4. Confirm i

right-click opens the very same native menu.
3. Choose **Delete session**.
4. Confirm in the dialog.
The new entry sits in its own section after "Copy Session ID".
If you delete the session you are currently viewing, the main view immediately opens a fresh empty s
ession in the same workspace, so the chat pane never sits on a deleted record.
If an individual cleanup step fails (a cache file held open, say), the session is still removed and
the UI reports "Session removed, but N item(s) could not be cleaned up". The failing entries are log
ged to the console so you can chase them one by one.

Dry run is the default, and that matters: every step before `--apply` is reversible, and nothing aft
s the default, and that matters: every step before `--apply` is reversible, and nothing after it is.
## How it works
The plugin ships two halves, both declared in the `dsh` field of `package.json`.
**Host half** (`lib/`) registers one named HTTP route, `POST /session-delete/api`, taking `{ "op": "
delete", "sessionId": "…" }`. The delete logic depends on zero official npm packages — every host ca
pability is pulled softly off the Cordis service object, with a plain filesystem fallback. That mean
s it works even when the profile cannot resolve the official `node_modules`.
The route has two gates at the door: POST only, and same-origin/loopback only (loopback peer, or a l
ocalhost `Host` with an `Origin` that is absent, `null`, `app:`, or same-origin). Everything else ge
ts a 403, so no arbitrary web page can CSRF you into deleting files.
**Browser half** (`client.js`) registers a menu item into `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` and
a confirm dialog into `shell.overlay`. The right-click handler does not build a second copy of the
menu — it locates the ellipsis button at the end of that row and synthesizes one `click()`, letting
the host's own `Menu` component open. Items, shortcuts, separators, and permission checks are all th
e native ones, so nothing drifts as the host evolves.

## Compatibility

- Node.js ≥ 18 (uses `node:test`, `fs.rmSync`).
- DSH ≥ 0.2.0. The host half hard-depends on `webSer
ver` only; `sessionPersistence`, `sessions`, `agents`, and `workspaceRegistry` are all soft-resolved

. Missing ones skip their step instead of killing the route.
- Works in both the desktop app and the
web UI. Desktop requests are recognized via `app:` origins.
Path encoding (`encodeSegment` / `projectKey`) is a **same-rules reimplementation** of the identical
ly named functions in the official persistence backend, not an import — that is what lets the plugin
compute the same directory without the official `node_modules`. If a host upgrade changes the namin
g scheme, the fallback path will compute the wrong directory; prefer the backend's `locate()` in tha
t case, or open an issue.
